_comment: DESIGN.md §11.5. Sends cost gems, add a monster to a target opponent's next wave, and grant the sender permanent passive income in gold. The defender always gets the kill bounty. ONE MONSTER PER SEND, and the send is NAMED AFTER IT: a tap used to buy a whole pack under a product name - 'Swarm Probe' for six swarmlings - which made every send a decision about a pack, and left the button saying its own name and then the monster's underneath. One tap buys one body, the button says which body, and the line under it says what that body does when it arrives. A send id therefore matches the monster id it delivers, which is the same word in two separate namespaces (defs.sends and defs.monsters) and reads correctly in both. Costs and income were divided by the old pack sizes, so the gems and gold per monster are exactly what they were. Placeholders, like every number in data/.
_tuning: THE SEND LADDER IS THE ECONOMY’S FLOOR. The cheapest send sets the best rate in the game - 10 gems per +1 gold a wave - and every dearer send is paying the difference for a stronger body or an ability, never for a better rate. Gems per income climbs 10, 11, 12, 14, 16 up the ladder, so an early swarmling is the correct economic move and a late bloater is a weapon that happens to pay a little. docs/BALANCE.md computes the whole run against that floor, so repricing a send here moves the budget every unit is priced against.
_vision: §12: the Revenant raid is the only send that grants sight, because vision has to be paid for. It used to ride along on the cheap probe as well, which made the efficiency floor strictly better than a pure economy send and left nothing to choose.
_abilities: §11.5, extended. Three of the five sends hand an ability to every monster they deliver (abilities.json), which is what makes a send a THING rather than a quantity of monsters: the same husk that walks in with a wave arrives braced when it is paid for. Putting the difference on the send rather than on a duplicate monster definition means one entry to tune and no second husk to keep in step with the first. The probe and the grub pack carry nothing - they are economy, not attacks.
